confident_false_claims: A `tools: Agent(worker, researcher)` entry limits which agents a subagent may spawn. The sub-agents doc says the type list in parentheses is ignored in a subagent definition; the allowlist applies only to an agent run as the main thread with `claude --agent`.
unsupported_claims: 'Claude delegates more' on Opus 5-generation models. The Agent SDK subagents doc says the claude_code preset adds a line telling Opus 5 not to call the Agent tool unless asked, which points the other way inside Claude Code.
statusline-setup is listed as a new built-in agent since fall 2025; it appears to predate that.
1.rationale: Covers all four core changes accurately: wizard removed in v2.1.198, background by default, forks via /subtask with fork mode on since v2.1.232, and nesting to depth 3 with CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH. It also gets the 20-subagent concurrency cap, the Task-to-Agent rename, the new frontmatter fields, the Explore model change (including the Fable detail) and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS right. It loses points for the false Agent(type) allowlist claim and the questionable delegation claim.

2.rationale: Accurate and current throughout. It covers the wizard removal, live reload, `claude plugin validate .claude/agents`, the claude agents distinction, background by default, fork mode with /subtask and its env var, nesting to 3 levels, SendMessage resume, extended-thinking inheritance, managed and --agents agents, the 20-subagent cap, the 15k description warning and trust-gated frontmatter hooks. Both cited issues (#72945, #29677) are real and relevant. Its only gaps are the Explore model change and nesting configuration details.

confident_false_claims: Lists `run_in_background` among the Agent tool's current inputs. With fork mode on, the interactive default since v2.1.232, Claude Code removes that parameter.
unsupported_claims: With agent teams on, 'any named Agent call' launches a teammate. The docs limit this to calls from the main conversation and exempt forks and calls that pass isolation.
3.rationale: Correct on all the core changes, with verified extras: the Agent(model:opus) rule form, the tools stripped from every subagent, the Explore model change, Pro/Team Standard defaulting to Opus since 2.1.280, the claude_code preset's Opus 5 no-delegation line, and issue #34692 closed as not planned. It has a couple of small inaccuracies or overgeneralizations and doesn't mention live reload of agent files.

confident_false_claims: /agents still creates and edits agents; the wizard was removed in v2.1.198.
Subagents still can't spawn subagents; nesting has existed since v2.1.172, with a default depth of 3 since v2.1.219.
Explore runs on Haiku; since v2.1.198 it inherits the session model, capped at Opus.
Background subagents request permissions up front and auto-deny anything not pre-approved; they now surface prompts in the main session.
4.rationale: Presents fall-2025 behavior as current. It contradicts three of the four core changes and hits two red flags: it says /agents is still the wizard and that subagents can't nest. It also omits background-by-default and forks. It gets some frontmatter fields, the Task-to-Agent rename and --agents right.

unsupported_claims: A `>`/`|` YAML block scalar counts as malformed frontmatter. Block scalars are valid YAML, and the docs don't say this.
Synced copies don't expand any `${CLAUDE_*}` variable. The docs name only ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} and ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}.
1.rationale: Gives the full Claude Code field list, the 1,536-character combined cap, the 1% listing budget with least-used descriptions dropped, silent ignoring of unknown keys, allowed-tools as turn-scoped and not trust-gated, and the 5k-token compaction keep. For claude.ai it has the six-key hard error, the name and description rules and the outdated Help Center 200-character limit. It also covers one-way sync with anthropic-skills naming and the Enterprise scan/review default from 2026-10-02, all of which I verified. Two small claims are unsupported.

2.rationale: Accurate and current. It gives the full field list (spec fields accepted but not acted on), the 1,536 cap with skillListingMaxDescChars, the 1% budget with skillListingBudgetFraction or SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET, skillOverrides name-only, and /doctor and /skill-doctor. On claude.ai it has the six-key hard error, the name rules including the folder-name match, the 1,024-character description, ZIP packaging under Customize > Skills, Share/Publish and sync back into Claude Code. 3.rationale: Complete and correct on every core point: the v2.1.3 merge, all fields optional with description defaulting to the first non-empty line, the full field list, silent ignoring of unknown keys, `claude plugin validate .claude` (valid per the CLI reference), the 1,536 cap with its setting, the 1% budget and compaction behavior. For claude.ai it has the six-key hard error including package_skill.py and the name and description rules. confident_false_claims: The skill listing budget is roughly 2% of the context window with a 16k-character fallback. It is now 1% (skillListingBudgetFraction default 0.01).
Nothing syncs between claude.ai, Claude Code and the API. Skills enabled on claude.ai sync into Claude Code sessions (v2.1.273+).

It states the stale 2% budget and the outdated 'nothing syncs' claim as current. It is unsure of the 1,536 per-skill cap, can't say whether claude.ai rejects unknown keys (it does, with a hard error) and omits several current frontmatter fields.

Its portal steps, review and auto-publish behavior, auth (claude.ai paid plan, Owner or Directory permission, connected GitHub, GitHub App for private repos), the retired Console form, the 10 submissions per 24 hours limit, @synced, the nightly community mirror and the v2.1.275 self-hosted route all check out against the claude.com and code.claude.com docs.

1.rationale: The right recommendation, with verified specifics: a private marketplace plugin, a sensitive userConfig stored in the OS keychain, and managed extraKnownMarketplaces and enabledPlugins in Organization settings > Claude Code > Managed settings (force-enable, hourly refresh, no per-group targeting, only server-managed reaching the web). Guardrails live in managed hooks with the mod caveats. What cloud sessions load is accurate, including .mcp.json in single-repo sessions only, as is the shared-environment secret risk. It also covers managedMcpServers (v2.1.259), autoUpdate locking, canary marketplaces through endpoint-managed settings, and the plugin_loaded OTel event. It flags its unconfirmed points honestly.

2.rationale: Equally strong and fully verified: plugin layout with the bin/ caveat, sensitive userConfig plus `claude plugin configure`, an OAuth org connector as the better route, and managed settings as the only managed source that reaches cloud sessions. It notes repo settings need trust and are ignored in the cloud, that force-enabled plugin hooks are exempt from allowManagedHooksOnly, that mods can't override managed hooks, and that `gh auth setup-git` is needed for silent background updates. Cloud token handling (no API credentials on Team/Enterprise, use a personal environment), org sync to @synced and the `claude doctor` managed-settings check are also correct.

confident_false_claims: Recommends making sure each repo's committed settings declare the plugin so it works on the web. Cloud sessions don't install plugins declared in a repo's .claude/settings.json.
3.rationale: The packaging, guardrails in managed settings (allowManagedHooksOnly, deny rules), the OAuth or env-var token options and the update advice are reasonable. The web guidance hits a red flag, it hedges on userConfig and on server-managed settings, and it never says that server-managed settings are what reach cloud sessions. Vendoring hooks and skills into each repo is offered only as a fallback.

unsupported_claims: Implies an MDM-deployed managed-settings.json is also how the setup reaches the web; only server-managed settings reach cloud sessions.
4.rationale: Sound and mostly current: a plugin with a sensitive userConfig, managed marketplace and plugin keys, and a correct list of what cloud sessions load and ignore. It recommends an OAuth org connector for subscription users and allowManagedModsOnly, and covers version precedence, validate and eval in CI, Tool Search with the 2,048-character cap, and the real Plugin4Shell SHA-pin attack. It is imprecise on MDM versus the web and doesn't spell out force-enable or the allowManagedHooksOnly behavior.

Its server-side recommendations are strong. The only slip is the minor error about the issue's status.

Setup covers the size guideline (medium, small on Pro), pre-allowed tools, the Pro /config toggle, piloting with /workflows, and saving to .claude/workflows.

It recommends a dynamic workflow with verified limits (16 concurrent, adjustable to 256, and 1,000 per run), resumability, saving, and the docs' own audit example, and contrasts subagents and agent teams correctly. Its practical steps cover the inventory, a rubric, two independent verifiers, the unrestricted size guideline, the Large workflow warning, pre-allowed tools, a `Workflow(name)` allow rule for -p in CI, Pro enablement, and a sensible caveat on what 'verified' means.
